questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had a couple of friends in the area who sold Boston to me and made it sound like a great opportunity. Furthermore, I am interested in linguistics and Boston is infamous for its local accent.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was awesome! I got to experience going to an American university for a semester and I was able to explore New England.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. I would have liked a bit more info about how to pay the host university for accommodation etc. but ultimately it worked out.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an introductory seminar with some information which was helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Could have used a bit more specific info. A little less "what to see in Boston" and a little more "this is how you can do this practical and necessary thing"

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I was asked to rank my wishes in terms of type of rooms etc. However it seemed kinda pointless as they just give the exchange students whatever is leftover, which is honestly fine.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There are 4 dining halls on campus open from 7am to 9/10pm. There are a number of meal plans to choose from. I had the unlimited one - big mistake. Choose at most the plan with 14 meals a week. You will get sick of the dining hall even though the food tastes fine.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Try to get essentials a few days before move-in day. There are a million universities in Boston and everything will be sold out because everyone moves in at the same time.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was fine. I was in a triple which was challenging at times but it was part of the experience.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was easy. I was ready during the timeslot they gave me and it wasn't an issue at all.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I checked the course catalog ahead of time and then added the courses I wanted to a planner and when it was time to register, I just did so from the planner. Super easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: BU provided me with a guide.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Check out the courses ahead of time. Plan ahead. Be ready when it is your time, since exchange students get the lowest priority for choosing classes.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was great. I really enjoyed my classes.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took onto intro to 101 level class in computer science and two 3rd year classes in linguistics which is closer to my normal field. I enjoyed being able to select from a wide and long list of courses and electives. The academic level was different than what I am used to from CPH. There's a lot more busywork and less reading. I never really felt stressed out though. It was not that difficult.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There was a mix of discussion sessions (holdseminar) and lectures which was similar. Different assignments counted as a percentage of your final grade which meant that my final exams only counted for 25% of the grade which was very different.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Intro to computing CS101
Phonetics and Phonology LX 301
Language Variation and Change LX346

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Phonetics and Phonology was great if you are interested in linguistics. It gave great insight into American English. There was another exchange student from a different country in that class as well.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I took some weekend trips to DC and NYC which cost money but it was worth it.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and housing were incredibly expensive. I paid 10k DKK a month to live in a triple. It was a lot.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Lots of options. They do an event called Splash where you can meet all of the clubs.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything you can imagine. European club, Girls who code club, choir, queer club, student government etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you are queer, the queer club was pretty good!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: You can get a weekend ticket for the commuter rail for 10 usd and it is a great deal!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy. I've previously lived in Canada so I am used to North America.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the clubs! Get to know people in your classes! I made a lot of local friends through my roommate, my classes, the clubs. It's easy if you are open. American are very talkative and friendly.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Americans are kinda direct and will speak to strangers in public. It was fine once I got used to it though. I had some issues with one of my roommates though as she was a freshman and very homesick and would talk on the phone for hours everyday. I think I just got unlucky with her specifically though.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: It is a lot more diverse which means I got to meet people from different cultures. People were also very very interested in my cultural background and things I would tell them about Denmark. Americans are very welcoming aa well. I got invited to two thanksgivings and went with an American classmate/friend to NY for thanksgiving with her family. Another friend drove me to the airport. If you are open to it, it is easy to make friends.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be open and say yes to things! Take trips, use your weekends and don't just stay in your dorm room. Don't get the unlimited dining plan.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I can recommend getting an American bank account and phone number. It will just make your life easier. A lot of Americans prefer texting and do not use whatsapp or messenger. I had Rockland Trust as my bank and they were great and helpful. I had Verizon for my phone plan which was super expensive but their coverage was good. You can probably find a better deal though.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I met some incredible people and saw some incredible places. It was truly amazing. I got to volunteer at a linguistics conference too which was so fun.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Sharing a room with someone who I was not really compatible with. I was great friends with the other roommate though and it ultimately worked out.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: BU is a great school! I really loved it. Challenges seemed small compared to how much fun I had. Boston is a beautiful city full of culture and history. I really do recommend it.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
